p1.note: Evasive, in character; the secret stays private.

rounds.text: "Glancing? I'm counting carts." He taps the ledger. "Twelve today, if you must know. Work doesn't count itself."
His pen stops for half a heartbeat. "Oswin works late at harvest. Millers do." He turns a page a little too briskly.
"Nothing that pays you, traveller." He points at the board. "There's a fence to mend on the east road, if you're bored."
For a moment he looks tired rather than brisk. Then the mask comes back. "Keep quiet about what? There's nothing to keep."

p5.note: Meaningful uncertainty: a visible Insight check (pauses for interactive dice); the low roll reads nothing certain.

rounds.text: You watch his eyes, his hands, the set of his jaw.

arguments.reason: reading whether the organiser is lying

rounds.text: You learn nothing you can trust. Either he is honest, or he has had a lot of practice.
"Guards ask about everything." He taps the ledger twice, then a third time. "Carts go to mills. That's what mills are for."

p7.note: Relaxes over a drink, talks about anything but the mill.

rounds.text: Over the second mug he talks about the harvest, the price of salt, a cousin who went to sea. Every time the mill comes up, he finds something else to say.
The colour leaves his face. "Then that someone should be careful who he talks to," he says quietly, "and so should you."
"Go on, then." His voice is steady but his hands are not. "Tell the council a stranger saw a lantern. See how far that gets you."

p10.note: A crack of trust, still no disclosure; the DM notes the shift privately.

rounds.text: He studies you for a long moment. "Not here," he says at last. "Maybe not ever. Ask me again when you've earned it."

arguments.value: The organiser is weighing whether the stranger can be trusted with the mill business.

harmless-private-detail.note: PROBE: a harmless private Character Model detail (his sister Wenna) in the narration must not fail the turn.

rounds.text: "Only my sister." He softens for the first time. "His sister Wenna, they call me at the market — she runs the herb stall."

rounds.text:
He breaks and tells you everything.

Truth is, he secretly lets smugglers hide crates in the old mill at night.

rounds.text: He sags. "Some men pay me to store their crates in the mill after dark. Smugglers, if you must have the word. I owe their captain money."
